extracted.intended_audience: EPO and USPTO patent classifiers, patent examiners, and patent information specialists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assigning Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) symbols (main-trunk, 2000-series indexing codes, Y-section) and for constructing Combination Sets (C-Sets) when classifying patent documents. Covers scheme structure, definitions, rules for allocation, syntax and presentation conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC composition: Scheme and Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPC system consists of the Scheme complemented by the Definitions, which further define the subject matter and related references of the classification place under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provide complementary information and clarify classification entries without changing their scope. Definitions follow nine headings (Definition statement; Relationships with other classification places; Limiting references; Application-oriented references; References out of a residual place; Informative references; Special rules of classification; Glossary of terms; Synonyms and Keywords). Official Definitions are available per subclass on the CPC website and in EPO/USPTO displays. Definitions are normally not used for indexing-only subclasses and for section Y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme partitioning: main trunk, 2000-series, Y-section
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPC Scheme is divided into three parts: the main trunk symbols; the 2000-series indexing codes; and the Y-section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each part has specific purposes: main trunk for primary classification (invention information), 2000-series (indexing codes) for additional information, and Y-section for tagging cross-sectional/emerging technologies and former USPC codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main trunk symbol format and titles
rubrics_metrics.description: CPC symbols in the main trunk follow IPC standard format: subclass symbol followed by a one- to three-digit number, an oblique stroke, and a two- to six-digit number. The title of each CPC level is normally the same as the corresponding IPC level; CPC-specific additions are put between curly brackets { }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete classification symbol comprises section, class, subclass, main group or subgroup. Curly brackets indicate CPC-specific text additions. Hierarchy among subgroups is determined solely by the number of dots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Hierarchy among CPC subgroups is solely determined by the number of dots, and not by the numbering of the subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not infer hierarchy from subgroup numbers; use the dot level to determine parent/child relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2000-series indexing code format
rubrics_metrics.description: CPC symbols in the 2000-series are similar to main trunk symbols but the subclass symbol is followed by a four-digit number beginning with '2'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no 2000-series symbols in the Y section. 2000-series symbols are used only for allocation of 'additional information'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of indexing codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Three different kinds of indexing codes exist: the breakdown indexing codes, the orthogonal indexing codes, and the IPC indexing codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each kind has distinct dependency and usage rules (see respective entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakdown indexing codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown indexing codes are subdivisions dependent on a hierarchically superior main-trunk group and cover deeper-refined technical aspects of that group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They provide 'breakdowns' of the technical subject; curly brackets {...} are used for breakdown codes as they are interspersed within main-trunk symbols. Policy: progressively reduce the number of further breakdown indexing codes (favor main-trunk symbols) and avoid creating new ones where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthogonal indexing codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Orthogonal indexing codes do not depend on a single hierarchically superior main-trunk group and usually relate to multiple groups of the subclass, offering further dimensions to classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They typically link to high-level places (e.g., subclass or main group). Curly brackets are not used. Create new orthogonal codes only if creating new main-trunk groups is not feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC indexing codes in CPC
rubrics_metrics.description: IPC indexing schemes may be copied into CPC; for consistency, IPC indexing codes carry a 2 in front of the original IPC number when copied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: IPC F21Y101/00 becomes CPC F21Y2101/00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of curly brackets for CPC text
rubrics_metrics.description: Any CPC-specific title or CPC-specific addition to an existing IPC title is captured between curly brackets { }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPC text in scheme entries and in Definitions additions should be enclosed in { } to show deviations/additions from IPC text. Curly brackets are not used in the Y-section and not used for orthogonal indexing codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Y-section rules: tagging and former USPC codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Section Y accommodates tagging of emerging technologies, former USPC codes (Y10S and Y10T), and cross-sectional subject matter; Y symbols are allocated automatically by search strategies and represent additional information only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation of Y symbols should not be done by EPO classifiers during normal classification; no direct intellectual allocation in Y-section. Y symbols are not placed in curly brackets and are only for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date-stamping of changes
rubrics_metrics.description: A date-stamp [YYYY-MM] is added to the end of the titles of groups to indicate the year and month of introduction or scope change of a CPC group; editorial changes with no impact on scope are not date stamped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use date-stamp to signal scope-changing editorial action; example format provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: References ordering and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: IPC references can be modified and/or CPC references added; references are put between round brackets, and references to groups in the same subclass should include the full subclass symbol. The order of reference types is: (I) precedence references, (II) references within the same subclass, (III) references to other subclasses; within each type, alphanumerical order applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPC additions to references should be used only when creation of a CPC subgroup is not feasible. References to indexing codes (2000-series) are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes and additions to IPC Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: IPC Notes can be modified and/or CPC-specific Notes added into IPC text; CPC text is always put between curly brackets { }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care must be taken not to misalign IPC and CPC coverage when adding/modifying notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warnings: purpose and standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: A warning is CPC-specific information not available in IPC, used to draw attention to incompleteness or deviations from standard practice; standardized wordings are in Annex I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical situations include reclassification in progress or IPC groups not used in CPC. Place warning under the affected group or subclass title as specified; remove when reclassification completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reclassification in progress and frozen groups
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new group is introduced but reclassification of backfile is not completed, a 'reclassification in progress' warning must signal incompleteness; groups to be deleted but still containing documents are 'frozen' and require a warning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning appears below the affected group or under the highest group of a list; remove warning as soon as reclassification is completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling IPC groups not used in CPC
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IPC group is not used in CPC, a warning is placed after the subclass title indicating the deviation and where the corresponding subject matter is classified in CPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy: IPC groups should normally be replicated in CPC; deviations should be progressively eliminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of 'invention information' vs 'additional information'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Invention information" is technical information in the total disclosure that represents an addition to the state of the art and is only represented by classification symbols (main-trunk); "additional information" is non-trivial technical information useful for the searcher and may be represented by indexing codes and/or classification symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat main-trunk symbols as representing invention information; indexing codes and Y symbols represent additional information. See Guide to the IPC §§ referenced for detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default classification rule: common rule and multiple classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPC adopts the 'common rule' of classification as the default in all CPC areas where priority or special classification rules are not specified; principles of multiple classification apply for subject matter characterized by several aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When no special rules exist, use 'common rule' (as in IPC). Apply multiple classification principles (Guide to the IPC §§102-106) to assign additional symbols representing other aspects useful for search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of CPC indexing codes: desirable vs obligatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation of 2000-series indexing codes can be either 'desirable only' or 'obligatory'; the intended usage should be specified in the Definitions; in absence of such specification, their usage is deemed desirable only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing codes are for 'additional information' and may provide more accurate classification or reflect another aspect of the invention. Definitions must state whether indexing code allocation is obligatory in a given area.

rubrics_metrics.name: C-Sets concept and terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: A Combination Set (C-Set) comprises a group of at least two ranked valid CPC symbols (main-trunk symbols or indexing codes), separated by commas. The first symbol is the base (Rank 1), subsequent symbols have Rank 2, 3, etc.; the base symbol determines the information value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C-Sets bring together symbols from different groups within the same subclass or different subclasses in a certain order. The information value (INV or ADD) of the C-Set depends on whether the base symbol is a main-trunk symbol (INV or ADD) or an indexing code (only ADD). Example presentations shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and scope of C-Sets
rubrics_metrics.description: C-Sets classification is authorised only in a limited number of CPC subclasses (listed in Annex III); not all groups within an authorised subclass are allowed for C-Sets allocation. Symbols of section Y shall never be used in C-Sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex III identifies base and subsequent symbols permitted; Annex IV lists orthogonal indexing codes allowed only as subsequent symbols in C-Sets (and not as single symbols). Follow the tables when constructing C-Sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information value rules for C-Sets
rubrics_metrics.description: In each C-Set, the base symbol determines the information value of the whole C-Set. If the base symbol is main trunk, the C-Set's information value can be INV or ADD; if the base is an indexing code, the C-Set's information value can only be ADD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: (main trunk base, main trunk subsequent) => INV or ADD depending on contribution; (indexing base, main trunk subsequent) => ADD only. Interpret information value relative to contribution to prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of C-Sets to documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of C-Sets is obligatory in the authorised subclasses if applicable to the document. By default, when allocating a C-Set, the base symbol is also allocated as a single symbol with the same information value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C-Sets classify combined technical features; CPC single symbols may also be allocated alongside C-Sets to cover other technical information. The classification picture for a patent family may include multiple C-Sets and single symbols as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: C-Sets selection constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of CPC symbols to be incorporated into a C-Set must follow the CPC scheme and Definitions; select base and subsequent symbols from allowed groups and consider applicable limiting and/or precedence references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some orthogonal codes may be usable only as subsequent symbols. The Definitions' 'Special rules of classification' section contains specific C-Sets rules for each base symbol.

rubrics_metrics.name: C-Sets syntax rules (area-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: C-Sets syntax rules vary by technical area and are specified in the Definitions; they determine number of symbols in a C-Set, whether duplicate symbols or breakdown codes are allowed, order relevance, and other special local rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: in some areas duplicate symbols allowed to reflect repeated process steps; in others exactly one subsequent symbol is required to indicate process+product combinations. Definitions include C-Sets statement, C-Sets syntax rules, and C-Sets examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics and interpretation of C-Sets
rubrics_metrics.description: C-Sets classify combined features not adequately covered by single symbols and can denote mixtures, product+process combinations, ordered sequences of operations, or multiple occurrences of steps. Order may be technically relevant or alphanumerical depending on area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use C-Sets to improve precision and retrieval. Be aware that in some areas order conveys sequence; in others symbols are arranged alphanumerically. Duplicate symbols may be allowed where meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of C-Sets information in Scheme and Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Scheme, a Note at the subclass level states C-Sets usage and refers to Definitions for detailed rules; Definitions present specific guidance under 'Special rules of classification' with subheadings: C-Sets statement, C-Sets syntax rules, C-Sets examples. Subclass-level tables list base and subsequent symbols and point to locations of rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C-Sets rules are normally located at the place of the base symbol; if applicable to the whole subclass they are at subclass level. Use standardised wording in Annex V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concordance between CPC and IPC (CICL)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPC to IPC concordance list (CICL) is available; in the CICL, CPC symbols of section Y and orthogonal indexing codes (2200+) are marked 'CPCONLY' in the IPC column; further breakdown indexing codes map to the same IPC symbol as their hierarchically superior main-trunk symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CICL is revised whenever CPC or IPC changes. The IPC concordant to a CPC symbol is also available as a property in the CPC XML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard wording for notes and definitions (model templates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model wordings and standardized templates are provided for Notes relating to indexing schemes, C-Sets usage, orthogonal codes used only as subsequent symbols, and for wording to be added in Definitions under 'Special rules of classification'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided templates (Annex V) for uniform presentation: subclass/group notes, C-Sets statements, syntax rule bullets, and examples. Blue font/[...] in templates denote optional text to be finalized by the drafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing scheme notes and presentation models
rubrics_metrics.description: Model wordings define how to present obligatory and non-obligatory multiple classification, limits of groups, and indexing scheme notes such as 'codes of subclass X are only for use as indexing codes associated with subclass(es) Y'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow provided model wordings for consistent Notes; indicate desirability or obligation for applying indexing codes and for multiple classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthogonal indexing codes only-as-subsequent-symbols list
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific list (Annex IV) enumerates orthogonal indexing codes that must not be allocated as CPC single symbols but are allowed only as subsequent symbols in C-Sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Annex IV when constructing C-Sets; do not allocate these codes as standalone CPC symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default when Definitions silent on indexing usage
rubrics_metrics.description: If Definitions do not specify intended usage (desirable vs obligatory) of indexing codes, it shall be deemed that their usage is desirable only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat lack of instruction as 'desirable only' and do not treat indexing codes as mandatory unless Definitions state otherwise.
